⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever. Detained Without a Clear Reason. I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had.

CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time. We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward. But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed. We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law. Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.” The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong. Then the officer’s tone changed. He told us we had “two options”: 1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted. 2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam. Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.” Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules? At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel? Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money. What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning: 1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious? 2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing? 3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations? Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence. We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment. This will likely be our last visit to Batam. To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear.

POSSIBLE ACT OF BRIBERY/ CORRUPTION So last Friday (21/2/2025), three of us (mom, brother and me) was having our weekend trip to Batam. We arrived at Batam Center Ferry Terminal at 9am local time. While lining up for passport check, I was setting up my roaming to fill up the Visa of Arrival (VOA). There, I was being called by an immigration lady to the office and both my mom’s and my phone, together with my passport was being taken by the immigration lady. Then, she told me to wait outside of her office (it was 9.30am Batam time). Roughly after 20-30 minutes, she went of of her office room to attend another offencer, but when she saw me, she asked me “kamu ngapain disini?” twice because I was super clueless. Then I told her that my phone and passport was taken by her. She then rudely told me “ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu nggak apa salahmu?” I replied, “aku tadi lagi setting my roaming service to fill my VOA”. Then, she told me that roaming can be done after immigration outside. I then just remained silent and nod softly. She then went back into her room and ghosted me for not sure how many hours. While waiting for her action, I was just sat on the chair, not provoking nor asking for a release because I believe she just did her job. Then, there was a man sat right to me asking what happened. I told him that my passport and phones were taken by the officer. He then softly told me that he can offer help. Me being suspicious with the offer (I can sense that his help came with a tipping/side money, I replied him “nggak papa. Aku tunggu aja”). This man then left me and went for another offender (not directly but periodically he will come into the room). Bear in mind that throughout my wait, there were many offender after me that being released in less than 10 minutes waiting (one of them directly was with the guy who offered me help). Fast forward, I was being held in the waiting area, from 9am until 1.30pm. When I was about to be released, the lady officer told me to not use phone anymore while waiting for the immigration check. Me being frustrated being held that long without phone and passport, replied her with a single word, “maybe”. She got furious and proceed to reject my entry. I told her that “that’s okay. Just send me back to Malaysia cause I was mentally and physically drained from the wait”. While waiting for my return ferry, she came to me asking me to call my family. Apparently, when my ferry PIC informed my mom that I will be sent home for “rude” behaviour, my mum was asking the lady officer’s name from the ferry PIC, and wanted to report her for wrong accussation. I was being accused for playing my phone despite being warned twice by the other officer (in which, I was not being warned at all for the offense (if any). She then cleared my entry after hearing that my mom wanted to report her for possible act of corruption and misaccusation (because at 11.30am Batam time, my mom went into the waiting area to see me, and I told her that there was one local guy offered me for help). The last picture was the guy who offered me help, having a conversation with the lady officer. This posting was not to accuse the officer for act of corruption, but for the visitor to be more aware of this frequent incidences of “random check/using phone while in immigration” offense. Also, for the public authority to investigate the presence of the guy offering me help in the Batam Center Ferry Immigration office. Why were he in the office most of the time. Also to Ms Cia, you owned me my 4 hours time waiting like a stupid guy, and you don’t deserve my respect. 2

Pagi-Pagi ke sini untuk menyebrang ke spore. Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan salah satu gerbang utama bagi wisatawan dan pebisnis yang ingin menyeberang ke Singapura dan Malaysia. Sebagai pelabuhan internasional yang sibuk, tempat ini dikenal dengan suasana yang tertib dan kondusif, memberikan kenyamanan bagi para penumpang yang akan berangkat maupun yang baru tiba. Salah satu hal yang paling mencolok di Pelabuhan Batam Center adalah sistem antrian dan pengelolaan penumpangnya yang teratur. Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian. Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan. Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya. 0:04 +2 1

review: ⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever. Detained Without a Clear Reason. I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had.

review: Hey guys, it’s your favorite elite traveler back with another unfiltered review—and this time, we need to talk about the gatekeeping situation at the Batam Center Ferry Terminal. As an Indonesian who travels extensively, I am usually so proud to welcome international visitors to our beautiful country. But my recent arrival at Batam Center at 9:30 PM was, without exaggeration, an absolute NIGHTMARE. If this terminal is meant to be a major international gateway, the current reality is a total embarrassment to our national hospitality. Here is the raw truth about what you can expect if you land here late at night: 1. The Immigration Bottle-Neck (The Absolute Worst Part) Imagine an entire ferry of exhausted travelers arriving at 9:30 PM, only to find exactly one immigration officer working the counter. The inefficiency was mind-boggling. But the real vibe-killer was the officer handling the desk—an older woman named Ibu May. To say she was rude is an understatement. Unprofessional, highly inefficient, and frankly, throwing what I can only describe as a 5-year-old’s tantrum behind the desk. As an Indonesian, it broke my heart to watch her. She is single-handedly ruining the image of Indonesian hospitality for every international tourist standing in that excruciatingly long line. 2. Zero Digital Readiness Before you even get to the chaos inside, there is no coordination at the entrance. There are no QR codes shared or displayed at the entrance for required digital arrivals or health forms before you enter the terminal. Everyone is left scrambling in the dark, trying to figure out what they need to do. It’s clunky, outdated, and unacceptable for a major transit hub in 2026. 3. The Transport Monopoly Trap Once you finally escape the terminal, don't even think about opening your Grab or Gojek apps. The terminal strictly bans ride-hailing apps to protect their local taxi monopoly. Normally, I’m all for supporting local drivers, but the execution here is a safety and logistical hazard. Most of the drivers stationed there are very elderly, struggle to understand directions, and—unbelievably—do not know how to type into or use Google Maps to reach your destination. If you don't know the exact streets yourself, you are essentially stranded with a driver who can't navigate. The Verdict 🚨 Batam Center Ferry Terminal needs a massive wake-up call, urgent staff retraining, and a complete tech overhaul. To the management: please address the lack of personnel, the attitude of staff like Ibu May, and let ride-hailing apps in so travelers can actually get home safely. review: CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time. We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward. But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed. We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law. Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.” The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong. Then the officer’s tone changed. He told us we had “two options”: 1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted. 2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam. Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.” Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules? At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel? Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money. What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning: 1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious? 2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing? 3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations? Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence. We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment. This will likely be our last visit to Batam. To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear. 1

The terminal facility transitions completely away from the standard, utilitarian transport depots of the past. It functions instead as a bustling lifestyle and commercial anchor, directly integrated with high-end hotels like the Batam Marriott and a sprawling waterfront dining promenade. Arriving passengers can immediately step out into a vibrant culinary oasis famed for its premium seafood restaurants, chic cafes, and lively alfresco lounges overlooking the Singapore Strait. Inside, the terminal features a clean, beautifully air-conditioned concourse packed with convenient retail shops, money changers, and comfortable waiting bays. Because it effortlessly fuses cutting-edge logistical efficiency with top-tier hospitality and lifestyle amenities, Harbour Bay remains the absolute go-to choice for business executives, weekend holidaymakers, and frequent commuters seeking a premium, stress-free travel experience. 1

We went to Batam as a group of 3 couples over the Vesak Day weekend (29 to 31/5/2026) and chose Harbour Bay terminal since it's the nearest to I-hotel Nagoya. We arrived on 29/5 around 3pm (Indo time) & auto-gate was down. Quite a number of visitors had to be transferred to the manual queue, it was quite messy with no proper management of the queues for entry. Luckily the service was quite fast & efficient. On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. Harbour Bay ferry terminal used to be smooth & less chaotic..please ensure there are sufficient officers/staff stationed at strategic points/locations in the departure area to manage the crowds.

Waspadalah terhadap Porter Penipu!! Saat Anda tiba di pelabuhan dengan Grab atau mobil sewaan, Anda harus turun di lantai 3. Jika Anda membawa barang bawaan, porter yang mengenakan rompi oranye akan datang dan dengan paksa memuatnya ke kendaraan Anda. Anda sama sekali tidak boleh mempercayakan barang bawaan Anda kepada mereka pada saat ini. Mereka tidak berbicara bahasa Inggris; mereka mendorong barang bawaan Anda ke area pengambilan bagasi di lantai 1, dan menggunakan isyarat dan aplikasi penerjemahan, mereka menuntut Anda untuk membeli tiket speedboat. Saya berniat untuk naik Ro-Ro (roll-off/roll-off) sejak awal, jadi meskipun saya meminta mereka untuk membiarkan saya membawa barang bawaan saya, mereka tetap bersikeras. Karena tidak ada pilihan lain, saya pergi ke lantai 3 untuk membeli tiket speedboat, hanya untuk diberitahu bahwa saya harus membayar biaya penanganan bagasi sebesar 300.000 Rupiah. Dalam modus ini, yang seperti perampokan tanpa pisau, bukan hanya porter tetapi juga orang-orang berseragam keamanan ikut serta—sekelompok 7 atau 8 orang—yang dengan senang hati membagi uang yang mereka peras dari saya di antara mereka sendiri. Meskipun totalnya hanya sekitar 70.000 hingga 80.000 won, saya belum pernah melihat petugas berseragam secara terang-terangan menipu orang asing di Vietnam atau Filipina, jadi rasa suka saya terhadap Indonesia telah sepenuhnya hilang. Jika Anda orang Korea yang naik perahu dari sini ke Tanjung Uban di Bintan, jangan sekali-kali menyerahkan barang bawaan Anda kepada porter. Tongkat golf tampaknya menjadi target utama. Perahu cepat sekitar 10 menit lebih cepat, tetapi tidak memiliki ruang bagasi, jadi saya sarankan untuk menggunakannya hanya jika Anda tidak membawa barang bawaan.

Ini adalah pelabuhan domestik untuk penerbangan ke Tanjung Uban atau Tanjung Pinang di Bintan. Setelah keluar dari taksi, masuk ke gedung dan langsung berjalan lurus (jangan sekali-kali menuruni tangga). Dorong pintu kaca, dan Anda akan menemukan loket tiket. Pastikan untuk menyimpan tiket Anda; jangan membuangnya bahkan setelah naik kapal. Saya naik speedboat pukul 10:00 menuju Tanjung Uban, tetapi tidak berangkat tepat waktu; berangkat beberapa menit terlambat. Saat Anda naik, seorang karyawan akan mengambil bagasi Anda dan meletakkannya di haluan kapal; setelah semua orang naik, mereka akan membersihkan tangga di dalam kapal dan memuatnya ke ruang kosong. Setelah tiba, mereka akan menurunkan semua bagasi setelah semua orang turun. Perjalanan speedboat memakan waktu sekitar 15 menit; bahkan istri saya, yang mudah mabuk laut, tidak merasa mabuk laut. Saat kembali ke Batam, ikuti saja orang-orang yang turun bersama Anda. Abaikan saja pria yang berteriak "Taksi," "Taksi." Meskipun agak sulit, jika Anda melewati tempat parkir terbuka dan membawa koper berat Anda menaiki dua tangga tanpa eskalator, Anda akan sampai di tempat Anda turun dari taksi untuk pergi ke Bintan. Kemudian, jika Anda berjalan ke kiri (tidak terlalu jauh), Anda akan sampai di halte bus dengan tanda STOP. Itu adalah Grab Point. Dari sana, Anda bisa memesan Grab atau Gojek dengan harga yang bagus. Namun, kemungkinan besar akan ada pengemudi di sana yang menawarkan layanan "taksi". Harga yang mereka tawarkan mungkin sedikit lebih murah daripada Grab atau Gojek. Tapi jangan naik; Anda akan bepergian di dalam sauna yang panas terik (tidak ada AC, hanya dua kipas angin yang beroperasi), dan lampu peringatan akan menyala. Bahkan ketika saya menggunakan Papago untuk menerjemahkan dalam bahasa Indonesia menanyakan apakah ada masalah dengan mobil, dia pura-pura tidak mendengar. Saya dan istri saya memasang sabuk pengaman untuk pertama kalinya di Indonesia. Ketika kami sampai di tujuan dan saya protes, pengemudi itu hanya tertawa. Baru setelah saya menolak membayar dan terus mengeluh, dia akhirnya meminta maaf. Baik itu Bintan Tanjung Uban atau Tanjung Pinang, untuk tujuan terdekat, Anda bisa berjalan sedikit lebih jauh dari pelabuhan dan memesan Grab. Namun, Anda mungkin tidak akan bisa mendapatkan Grab untuk jarak jauh. Sebaliknya, saya bahkan tidak bisa mendapatkan Grab dari jarak jauh ke Tanjung Uban atau terminal Tanjung Pinang. Gojek bahkan tidak muncul di Bintan. Sebagai informasi, baik di Batam maupun Bintan, Anda tidak diperbolehkan naik taksi Grab atau Gojek di depan terminal. Siapa yang melakukan ini? Saya menduga itu adalah sopir taksi yang berbasis di terminal yang bertindak teritorial dan meminta tarif yang sangat tinggi.

Kejadian kemarin saat saya hendak pulang dari Batam ke Selat Panjang melalui Pelabuhan Sekupang. Saat tiba di pelabuhan, saya menuju konter yang jelas-jelas bertuliskan “Dumai Line” untuk membeli tiket. Setelah membayar dan menerima tiket, saya heran karena tiket yang diberikan ternyata bertuliskan “Batam Jet”. Saya kemudian bertanya kepada petugas, “Kok Batam Jet? Saya mau naik Dumai Line.” Namun petugas tidak menjawab pertanyaan saya dan hanya mengatakan, “Kapal besar.” Saya kembali menegaskan bahwa saya ingin tiket Dumai Line, tetapi petugas hanya diam. Lalu petugas lain mengatakan bahwa uang tidak bisa ditransfer kembali karena pembayaran sudah dilakukan. Untungnya akhirnya uang saya dikembalikan secara tunai. Setelah itu saya membeli tiket di konter Dumai Line yang sebenarnya, yang berada tepat di sampingnya, dan mendapatkan tiket yang sesuai. Yang membuat saya semakin kesal, ternyata orang tua saya pernah mengalami kejadian serupa. Karena tidak terlalu mengenal tulisan, mereka baru mengetahui tiket yang dibeli bukan Dumai Line saat sudah hendak naik kapal dan diberitahu oleh petugas. Saya sebenarnya tidak berniat memposting hal ini. Namun karena kejadian yang sama juga dialami oleh orang tua saya, saya merasa perlu menyampaikan keluhan ini. Mohon kepada pihak Pelabuhan Sekupang untuk menindaklanjuti dan mengawasi praktik seperti ini agar tidak ada lagi penumpang yang mengalami kebingungan atau dirugikan, terutama orang tua dan penumpang yang kurang memahami perbedaan loket maupun nama operator kapal. Terminal domestik melayani rute antarpulau seperti ke Karimun, Tanjung Balai, Dumai, dan pulau-pulau di wilayah Riau lainnya, sementara terminal internasional melayani rute cepat ke Singapura dan Malaysia dengan waktu tempuh sekitar 45 menit. Fasilitas di Terminal Feri Sekupang tergolong lengkap dan modern. Di dalamnya tersedia ruang tunggu berpendingin udara, loket tiket yang tertata rapi, area makan dan kafe, layanan money changer, ATM, serta musholla. Tersedia juga layanan transportasi darat seperti taksi resmi dan parkir kendaraan yang luas. Terminal internasionalnya bahkan dilengkapi dengan business lounge, Wi-Fi gratis, serta sistem imigrasi yang cepat dan efisien, menjadikannya alternatif favorit bagi penumpang yang ingin menghindari keramaian di pelabuhan Batam Centre. Selain fungsi utamanya sebagai pelabuhan penumpang, Terminal Feri Sekupang juga menjadi wajah kota Batam bagi wisatawan mancanegara. Dengan tampilan bangunan yang modern dan bersih, serta layanan yang semakin profesional, terminal ini memainkan peran penting dalam mendukung sektor pariwisata dan mobilitas masyarakat. Letaknya yang strategis di dekat kawasan pemukiman seperti Tiban, Batu Aji, dan Tanjung Riau juga menjadikannya pelabuhan pilihan bagi warga lokal maupun pelancong. 0:16 0:08 0:11

Beberapa speedboat berangkat dari sini ke Sumatra dan pulau-pulau sekitarnya. Kami naik satu ke Kuala Lumpur dengan harga 612.000 rupee yang lumayan mahal. Sayangnya, penerbangan ke Jakarta hampir lebih murah. Pelabuhannya sendiri sangat baik. Petugas di meja informasi ramah dan membantu. Staf di loket tiket agak terlalu bersemangat, tetapi kami tetap mendapatkan tiket. Ada restoran yang bagus di seberang jalan. Kapalnya penuh petualangan, cepat, dan stabil. Modelnya sangat tua, ditenagai oleh lima motor tempel yang luar biasa berisik, tetapi tampaknya bertenaga. Kami berangkat tepat pukul 10.00 pagi dan tiba di tujuan tepat pukul 17.00, termasuk istirahat makan siang selama setengah jam. Suara mesin dan pemutaran video yang terus-menerus keras dari ponsel sangat mengganggu. Orang-orang di sini tidak sopan dan tidak punya sopan santun. Setidaknya banyak dari mereka yang begitu. Bahkan beberapa awak kapal. Perjalanan menyusuri garis pantai hampir sepanjang perjalanan. Perahu berhenti beberapa kali dan menyeberangi sungai besar di pedalaman Sumatra. Hanya setengah jam terakhir yang membawa kami menyeberangi lautan lepas. Di Kuala Lumpur, kami disambut dengan hangat dan diizinkan berfoto selfie dengan pemuda setempat. Daerah ini sangat Muslim, dan kami harus mencari cukup lama sebelum sebuah hotel mau memberi kami kamar ganda tanpa perlu bukti pernikahan (meskipun kami sudah menikah selama 12 tahun). Kami tidak mengalami hal seperti itu di tempat lain di Indonesia.

I work in Singapore and I took my kids and in-laws(Visit pass holders) to Batam as it was a long weekend. It was a bitter experience where my family including 2 kids(2 and 6yo) were held inside a room with no proper reason for nearly 2 hours. We waited for 15 mins clueless and realized the supposed to be officer started eating his lunch, smoking and laughing with other workers without any sense that there were older people and small kids inside that small suffocating room and I actually felt that they are obliged to attend to us first or atleast give an explanation. After all, we were not there for any free service. I stepped out because of smoke and they demanded us to stay in. We were treated no less than criminals and were literally ill treated. After an hour a guy came in and finally, I understood that they presumed that we were there for Visa extension. I was asked why we didn’t go to Malaysia, after all it was my choice to do whatever I wish and it is never mentioned anywhere in the immigration guidelines. They asked for 100$ to let us go after 1.5 hours. I asked them the passports back so that we can return, which they never did. Later, head of the immigration came, got our passports stamped and got our money back and apologised. I felt they were so racist and had some cold attitude to people from India. I will never go back again. Totally hate it, forget being an educated officer, these people are so insane that they should learn how to treat fellow human beings.
